correctness.rationale: Every three-symbol source has at most three distinct two-symbol deletion outputs, so at least six are required for all sixteen ordered targets. The six-word construction in Chee–Ge–Ling Table 6.1 attains the bound. A C++17 lexicographic six-subset census and a separately implemented Python uncovered-target branching census are both complete by their respective justified capacity tests; the two lists of valid six-sets match exactly at 644. All 48 alphabet-permutation/reversal images were computed for each codebook; resulting orbit sizes 8,12,24,48 occur 1,3,9,8 times, totaling 644. The deletion-shadow size excess distribution is exactly 120,336,188 for 0,1,2; zero excess iff the covering shadows partition all 16 targets, so 120 are perfect. Executable reproducer checked both catalogs on the actual delivered paths and reported VERIFY_OK twice. The counts concern only q=4, length 3, six distinct codewords.

value.rationale: Four symbols model the natural nucleotide alphabet. The six-word covering optimum is the first small design requiring multiple shadows to cover all ordered pairs; its entire solution layer, rather than an arbitrary sample, is a motivated mathematical object. The exact 644 labeled, 21 orbit-class enumeration, and the 120-versus-524 perfect/nonperfect split reveal substantial structural variation and distinguish coverage from deletion-error correction. A complete catalog with representatives and reproducible independent exhaustive enumeration is directly useful for choosing distinct minimal designs. The contribution is not a re-derivation of the known minimum size.
